name: Visceral Arteriovenous Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Visceral AVM

criteria.description: Demonstration of abnormal direct arteriovenous shunting within visceral organs on angiography or contrast-enhanced imaging
Presence of symptoms such as gastrointestinal bleeding, abdominal pain, or portal hypertension attributable to AVM
Exclusion of other vascular malformations or neoplastic causes by clinical and imaging evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging-confirmed visceral arteriovenous shunting plus compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging modalities such as CT angiography, MRI, or catheter angiography.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal bruit over affected visceral region
pathognomonic.notes: Audible turbulent blood flow due to arteriovenous shunting

pathognomonic.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure secondary to AV shunting
searchTerms: heart failure with increased blood flow
high-output heart failure from abnormal blood vessels
heart strain due to blood vessel shunting

common.notes: Often due to mucosal ischemia or rupture of abnormal vessels
searchTerms: ongoing blood loss in digestive tract

common.symptomName: Abdominal pain localized to involved organ
common.notes: Due to ischemia or mass effect
searchTerms: pain in belly over affected organ

common.notes: Secondary to altered portal blood flow
searchTerms: enlarged spleen and high blood pressure in liver veins
signs of portal hypertension including spleen swelling
increased pressure in portal vein with splenomegaly

occasional.notes: Resulting from portal hypertension or liver involvement

searchTerms: low red blood cells from bleeding
anemia due to chronic blood loss

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to anemia or heart failure
searchTerms: tiredness from anemia or heart problems
fatigue related to low red blood cells or heart failure
weakness due to blood or heart issues

rare.notes: Due to compression by vascular malformation

laboratory: Anemia on complete blood count due to chronic bleeding
Elevated liver enzymes if hepatic involvement present
imaging: Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI showing early venous filling and nidus of abnormal vessels
Catheter angiography demonstrating direct arteriovenous shunting
Doppler ultrasound revealing turbulent flow and vascular dilatation
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; usually sporadic
Rarely associated with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) mutations
other: Physical exam may reveal abdominal bruit
Signs of high-output cardiac failure on cardiovascular examination

distinguishingFeatures: Benign vascular tumor with different imaging characteristics
Absence of direct AV shunting on imaging

redFlags: Sudden onset of massive gastrointestinal hemorrhage
Signs of high-output cardiac failure in young patients
Rapidly enlarging abdominal mass with bruit
references: Lee BB, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of arteriovenous malformations. J Vasc Surg. 2018;67(1):298-307.
